differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: NATS employs a straightforward publish-subscribe model, distributing messages directly to subscribed clients with minimal intermediaries for ultimate speed and simplicity.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ acts as a feature-rich message broker, managing queues, exchanges, and routing rules, offering advanced delivery guarantees and flexibility.

differences.title: 2. PROTOCOL
differences.leftDesc: Utilizes a custom, highly optimized text-based protocol for maximum performance and low latency, designed for extreme speed and minimal overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Adheres to the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP), providing a standardized, feature-rich, and interoperable messaging framework.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: NATS excels at high-volume, low-latency messaging, designed to handle millions of messages per second with minimal processing.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ offers robust throughput suitable for many enterprise applications, though it generally incurs higher latency due to its feature set.

differences.title: 4. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: NATS prioritizes ease of use and deployment with a minimal configuration surface, making it ideal for microservices and IoT.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ provides extensive configuration options for complex routing, message persistence, and delivery acknowledgments, requiring more setup.

differences.title: 5. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: NATS is perfect for real-time data streaming, telemetry, and command-and-control where speed and simplicity are paramount.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ is suited for decoupling services, implementing background job processing, and ensuring reliable delivery for business-critical operations.

differences.title: 6. CLUSTERING
differences.leftDesc: NATS uses a simple gossip protocol for cluster discovery and state synchronization, allowing for dynamic node additions and removals.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ typically relies on external tools or Raft for quorum and state management in clustered environments.

differences.title: 7. MESSAGE GUARANTEES
differences.leftDesc: NATS offers basic delivery guarantees. 'At-least-once' is default, with 'at-most-once' achievable via careful client logic.
differences.rightDesc: RabbitMQ provides robust message acknowledgment and persistence mechanisms to achieve reliable 'exactly-once' processing semantics.
